description: Jordaan 17th-18th c. narrow gable houses (Bloemgracht, Egelantiersgracht, Anjeliersstraat): 4-6.5 m fronts of dark red-brown brick, a ground storey and two or three upper storeys of 2.6-2.7 m, two axes under 4.6 m and three above; white sash windows with white sills; a neck gable (halsgevel) with one attic light and a hoist beam, or a bell gable (klokgevel), rising about 3.5 m over the gable foot

match.note: Bloemgracht 16-32, 80-128 (2024-12 strips): gable foot 8.6-8.9 m over a ground and two upper storeys, gable tops 11.3-12.5 m; BAG dates these fronts 1725-1865 (rebuilds and restorations), so the years are wide and the skyline crown decides between this type and the cornice house (crownMatch)

neck.note: Bloemgracht 80-128 (168157): a neck gable 8.8-12.3 m with one attic light and the hoist beam over it

bell.note: Bloemgracht 16-32 (173345): a bell gable 8.6-11.3 m, one attic light

door-left.note: house door on the left axis; a pand whose door reads on the right is mirrored (mirrorForDoor), so a two-axis front keeps a valid door bay

rhythm.groundFloor: a house door and windows, or a small shop
rhythm.roofline: neck or bell gable with one attic light and a hoist beam
schemaLimits: the sandstone scrolls (klauwstukken) beside the neck are not drawn
the gable cap ornaments are not drawn
